name: Bocas Town (Isla Colon)
tagline: The colourful, walkable heart of the archipelago
description: The main hub, a compact grid of colourful stilt buildings over the water on Isla Colon. Here you find most rentals, restaurants, cafes, dive shops, bars and the water taxi docks. It is lively, social and convenient, the natural landing point for first-time nomads and travellers.
bestFor: First-time visitors, nomads wanting cafes and convenience
pros: Widest choice of food, wifi and services
Easy water taxi links to every island
Best place to meet the nomad and backpacker crowd

name: Bluff Beach / North Isla Colon
tagline: Wild surf coast and quiet jungle beaches
description: The north of Isla Colon, reached by a bumpy road from town, is a string of wilder beaches including Bluff and Paunch. It draws surfers and anyone seeking quiet, nature and space, with jungle backing long sandy stretches and turtles nesting seasonally along this coast.
bestFor: Surfers and quiet-nature lovers who want to escape town
pros: Excellent surf breaks and empty beaches
Great for a slower, off-grid rhythm
cons: Rough road and far from town amenities

name: Isla Bastimentos (Old Bank / Red Frog)
tagline: Afro-Caribbean village life and postcard beaches
description: A short boat from town, Bastimentos blends the laid-back Afro-Caribbean village of Old Bank with famous beaches like Red Frog and jungle trails inland. It feels more local and less developed than Bocas Town, rewarding travellers who want culture, nature and a slower island pace.
bestFor: Culture seekers and beach-and-jungle slow travellers
pros: Stunning beaches and jungle trails nearby
Quieter and more affordable than Bocas Town

name: Isla Carenero
tagline: A two-minute boat hop to peace and surf
description: Just across the water from Bocas Town, Carenero offers calm, over-water cabins and small restaurants only a two-minute lancha ride from the action. It suits nomads who want quiet nights and easy water access while staying close enough to reach town whenever they like.
bestFor: Nomads wanting calm with quick access to Bocas Town
pros: Over-water lodging and a decent surf break
cons: Few shops or services on the island
